paper.title_en: A unified stochastic random walk theory for Kolmogorov spectrum, halo mass functions, and halo density profiles
paper.abstract_en: We develop a unified stochastic framework for nonequilibrium systems and apply it to turbulence and cosmic structure formation. Spectra and distributions evolve by transport in "scale space", described by random walks and Fokker-Planck equations with scale-dependent waiting times. We reformulate the turbulent cascade as a random walk in wavenumber space with waiting time $τ_{gk}\propto k^{-γ}$. With $γ=2/3$ fixed by self-consistency, we recover the Kolmogorov $-5/3$ law and obtain the full energy spectrum, including the inertial-dissipation crossover, exponential cutoff and spectrum constant, without applying dimensional analysis to the spectrum itself. In bottom-up hierarchical structure formation, low-mass haloes collapse early and retain primordial imprints, while prolonged assembly near the characteristic mass $m_h^*$ erases this memory and establishes a universal spectrum $P(k)\propto k^{-1}$. We model this as a random walk in halo mass space with $τ_g\propto m_h^{-λ}$. This yields a stretched Gaussian halo mass function that reproduces the Press-Schechter form, with small-scale scaling $f_M\propto m_h^{-λ}$ and an exponential cutoff at $m_h>m_h^*$, both set by $λ$. It also produces a double-$λ$ mass function: $λ$ reflects the primordial spectrum at low masses and approaches $2/3$ near $m_h^*$, where gravity dominates. For individual haloes, a spatial random walk with $τ_{gr}\propto r^{-γ}$ generates a double-$γ$ density profile that reproduces the Einasto profile, with small-scale scaling $ρ_r\propto r^{-2γ}$ and an exponential cutoff at $r>r_s$, both set by $γ$. Here $γ$ is fixed by the initial spectrum in the inner core and approaches $2/3$ ($ρ_r\propto r^{-4/3}$) in the gravity-dominated outskirts. This framework thus describes turbulent cascades and cosmic structure formation on a common footing.
